questions.question: Which of the following is the State Bird of Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Indian Bustard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan's state bird **is **the Great Indian Bustard.**
 
• It's a huge bird with long naked legs and a horizontal body.
 
• This species, which has an ostrich-like look, is the heaviest of the flying birds.
 
• Hunting and the degradation of its habitat, which comprises huge swaths of dry grassland and scrub, have made the species severely endangered. It is protected by India's **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972**.
 
• It, however, received no attention and remained BPL (Below Protection Line).​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Asian koel **is the state bird of Jharkhand.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's state bird is the** Sarus Crane**.
 
• **The Indian roller** is the state bird of Odisha, Telangana, and Karnataka in India.

questions.question: Article 40 of the Indian constitution, "Organisation of village panchayats", is a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:-**

 
 
• Articles 36-51 of Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). 
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable i.e non-enforceable in the court of law.
 
• They act as directives to the government to create any law.
 
• They act as the ‘instrument of instructions’.
 
• **Article 40 is with respect to the Organisation of village panchayats. (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duties:-

 
 
• ​These are a set of moral obligations that are mentioned in the Constitution of India.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• These duties are not enforceable by law but are expected to be followed by every citizen as a means of promoting a spirit of patriotism and upholding the ideals of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• Fundamental Rights:-
 
 
• FRs are known as the base of the Indian constitution & mentioned in Part III of the constitution.
 
• They prohibit unreasonable interference of the state & prevent its executive & legislature to become authoritarian, hence putting due limitations on state power.
 
 
 
• Legal right:-
 
 
• It is an interest accepted and protected by law.
 
• It is a claim that a person has against another person or against the state. Legal rights can be enforced through the courts.

questions.question: Which article of Indian Constitution talks about Advocate-General for the State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 165** of the Indian Constitution is related to the office of **Advocate General of State**.

 
 
• He is the** highest law officer of the state.**
 
 
 
• The appointment of the Advocate General is done by the Governor on the advice of the council of ministers of the state.
 
• The person who is eligible to hold the office of advocate general in India must meet the following criteria:
 
 
• He must be an **Indian Citizen.**
 
• He should be **eligible to be appointed as the judge of the High Court**; i.e. he must meet one of the following eligibility criteria:
 
 
• A barrister having experience of more than 5 years.
 
• A civil servant with an experience of more than 10 years along with an experience as a servant in Zila Court for at least 3 years.
 
• A pleader over 10 years in any high court
 
 
 
• He **shouldn’t be more than 62 years of age**, as is the age qualification for a High Court Judge.
 
 
 
• The Constitution **does not fix the term** of Advocate General in India. He remains in the office during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• The process and justifications for removing the Advocate General of State are not found in the Constitution. The **governor has the right to remove him or her at any time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duties and functions** of the **Advocate General of State**:

 
 
• When the governor directs him to counsel on legal concerns, it is his duty to advise the state government.
 
• In addition, he must carry out any legal responsibilities delegated to him by the state governor.
 
• He is obligated by the Constitution to carry out the tasks and responsibilities specified in it or in any other constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Article 145** of Indian Constitution deals with the **Rules of Courts,** etc.
 
• **Article 77** of Indian Constitution mentions the **Conduct of business of the Government of India**.
 
• **Article 136** of Indian Constitution addresses the **special leave to appeal by the Supreme court**.
 
 
• It means that, with the exception of military tribunals and court-martials, the Supreme Court is empowered to grant, at its discretion, special leave to appeal from any judgment in any case rendered by any court or tribunal within the borders of India.
 
 
 
• Attorney General of India:
 
 
• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, duties, and qualifications of the Attorney General of India.
 
 
• The Attorney General of India will be appointed by the President from among those who meet the requirements to be appointed as Supreme Court judges.
 
• The Attorney General will serve as long as the President so desires.
 
 
 
• He is the chief law officer in the country.
 
 
• He provides legal advice to the Government of India and represents the Government in legal matters.
 
• He also has the power to appear in any court of law in India and can take part in any proceedings that affect the Government of India.
 
• Thus he have the right of audience in all Indian courts while carrying out his duties.
 
 
 
• Under Article 88 of the Indian Constitution, he is free to participate in and speak at any session of the Houses of Parliament, as well as in any joint session, and to be appointed to any committee of the Parliament; however, he is not entitled to vote. 
 
• He is entitled to all the privileges and immunities that are granted to members of Parliament.

questions.question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The no-confidence motion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **No-confidence motion** is a statement or vote about whether a person in a position of responsibility is still deemed fit to hold that position.
 
• It is the most powerful weapon available to the Parliament to ensure **executive accountability**.
 
• If the motion is passed, it implies that the current government no longer has the support of the majority of the members of the Parliament.
 
• This can lead to the resignation of the Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers.
 
• The motion is typically moved by the opposition to challenge the government’s legitimacy and performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **No-confidence motion**
 A motion moved by a member of the Parliament expressing lack of trust in the government’s ability to govern.
 
 

 **Executive Accountability**
 The responsibility of the executive branch of government to the legislature and, through it, to the public.
 
 

 **Parliament**
 The supreme legislative body of a country, consisting of elected representatives.
 
 

 **Opposition**
 The political parties or groups that are not in power and challenge the government’s policies and actions.
 
 

 **Prime Minister**
 The head of the government in parliamentary systems, responsible for running the executive branch.

questions.question: Article 25 to 28 of the Indian constitution provide for _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Freedom of Religion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian constitution** provide for **the Right to Freedom of Religion**.
 
• This means that every citizen of India has the right to practice and propagate any religion they choose.
 
• This right also includes the freedom to manage religious affairs and institutions, as well as the right to own and acquire property for religious purposes.
 
• The Constitution also prohibits discrimination based on religion, and guarantees that every person has the right to access and attend religious institutions of their choice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Culture and Educational Rights: **Articles 29 and 30 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities. These articles ensure that minorities have the right to conserve their language, script and culture, and to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• **Right to Equality: **Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right to Equality. This right ensures that every citizen of India is equal before the law and has equal protection of the law. It also prohibits discrimination on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
 
• **Right against Exploitation: **Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right against Exploitation. This right prohibits trafficking in human beings, forced labor, and child labor. It also prohibits employment of children in hazardous jobs.
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion: **Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution provide for the Right to Freedom of Religion. This right ensures that every citizen of India has the freedom to practice and propagate any religion they choose. It also includes the freedom to manage religious affairs and institutions, and the right to own and acquire property for religious purposes.

questions.question: What is the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Panchayat Samiti.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Panchayat Samiti **is the** intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions.**
 
• It is the** tehsil or taluka or block level of the rural local-self government system** in India.
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the block level is an Administrative Authority that is responsible for enforcing the law and carrying it into effect.
 
• They form the middle level of the Panchayati Raj Institutions in India.
 
• It acts as a link between Village Panchayats (Gram Panchayats) and Zila Parishad (District council).
 
• It was formalized in 1992 by the 73rd amendment to the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.
 
• It stipulates that in states or Union Territories with more than two million inhabitants there are three levels of PRIs:
 
 
• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level
